title: Samsung could unseat SK Hynix as HBM leader in 2027
source_used: Digitimes (publisher preview only; article behind subscription)
key_facts: Digitimes preview: Samsung Electronics could overtake SK Hynix as the world's largest supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) in 2027.
Digitimes cites HBM4 prices climbing and memory makers competing for limited DRAM production capacity.
The statement rests on forecasts presented at an October 6 semiconductor industry forum in Seoul.
quote_evidence: Samsung Electronics could overtake SK Hynix as the world's largest supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) in 2027, as HBM4 prices climb and memory manufacturers compete for limited DRAM production capacity, according to forecasts presented at an October 6...
why_it_matters_hint: A change of leader in HBM would shift who supplies the memory that AI chips depend on, but this is a forecast and the details are not visible.
event_date: Forum on 6 Oct 2026; Digitimes report 12 Oct 2026
notes: Digitimes is behind a subscription; only the headline, one-sentence preview and page description could be read. No other outlet carrying the same forecast was found (three Google News searches). BigGo Finance (10 Oct 2026) separately reports Samsung's HBM revenue share rising from 21% to 33% in Q2 against SK Hynix's 50%, which is context only and not part of this entry.
